messages.content: France proposes non-aggression: I move south (Piedmont, Med), you secure north-central. We avoid Burgundy/Rhine conflict. Mutual benefit—leaves both strong against England's coastal threat.

Germany here. I'm moving KIE→HOL, BER→KIE, MUN→RUH to expand westward into neutral zones. Propose non-aggression through Fall 1901: neither attacks the other. You hold the south, I take the north and east. Fair terms?

Agreed. I hold north-central: Burgundy stays neutral, Rhine yours. I expand east into Silesia/Ruhr; you take south (Piedmont, Spain corridor). We coordinate against England's western push. Formal commitment?
Agreed. Non-aggression through Fall 1901. You secure north-central, I consolidate south and Mediterranean. Fair division of neutral spoils.
Confirmed. North-central secured. I'll watch England's expansion and ensure no single power dominates. We coordinate if he overextends.

Piedmont/Spain expansion accepted. But clarify: "coordinate against England" means what exactly? I won't attack England without provocation. And Burgundy staying neutral means neither of us enters it—confirm?
France opening: I claim south-west Mediterranean, you take Scandinavia/North. Germany isolated in center. Interested in coordinating against central expansion?

England to France. Early coordination advantages us both. I'll secure northern English Channel/North Sea (YOR, WAL); you take GAS and BUR southward. Germany cannot match our combined tempo. Non-aggression spring/fall?

France: Mediterranean expansion noted. I can't commit to formal anti-Germany pact—invites isolation if he falls. But: coordinate on Scandinavia denial, mutual non-aggression in Channel. That serves us both better.

Interested but cautious. Germany moving aggressively westward (HOL, RUH). I'll push into BUR/SPA to block their southern expansion. Non-aggression Spring, but Fall coordination depends on Germany's actual tempo—if they threaten you, I'm in.

France: I'm locking in Channel peace—F LON stays away from your coast. You secure BUR/SPA; I take Scandinavia and block Germany northward. Germany moving Silesia+Ruhr+Norway threatens us both. Coalition serves our growth better than isolation.
Agreed: mutual non-aggression in Channel (F BRE holds, no invasion). Scandinavia denial means neither of us supports Germany north. Seals a practical stalemate line.
England to Germany. Mutual benefit: I focus west (France, Low Countries); you take East (SIL, PRU, Scandinavia). We stay separate turns 1-3, both profit. Interested?
Germany. Moving west into Holland and Ruhr. I propose we avoid conflict this year while both expand against neutrals. Non-aggression through Fall 1901 works for both of us. Agree?
England, your offer is tempting but leaves France isolated against your coastal dominance. I'm committing to north-central expansion instead—Silesia/Ruhr/Scandinavia. Wish you success in the south.
Germany: Agreed. Non-aggression through Fall 1901. You take east, I'll develop west against France and expand north. Clear division serves both.
Confirmed. Non-aggression through Fall 1901. I take Silesia, Scandinavia, and eastern neutrals; you develop the west. Both benefit from clear zones.

Germany: Norway and Sweden are my sphere—North Sea is British advantage. Your Silesia/Ruhr focus makes sense. But Scandinavia grab forces me toward France alliance. Better outcome: you take PRU/SIL, I take NWY/SWE. Both expand cleanly, mutual non-aggression remains?
